cost: CLI config/queue reads are bounded; a watch iteration pays the core pass plus configured100–60000ms delay. No wall-clock throughput or continuous root-chat availability is established.
description: CLI parses prepare, launch, once, watch, status and bound report review commands. Config loading occurs before dispatch. Watch is one independent Rust process; it stops at a run-root STOP marker between passes, otherwise invokes one core pass and sleeps the configured interval. No arbitrary client program, prompt path or shell command is accepted.

inverse: Exclude unknown commands and wrong arities reaching a terminal action. Only prepare/launch explicitly create run/session state; watch never launches or adopts missing sessions. Root review does not apply code, admit annotations or train. A STOP marker does not promise interruption of an active model.

CLI JSON output is compatible with several earlier terminal histories, especially waiting and quarantined effects. A status value records durable job state and last redacted observation rather than proving the terminal is currently idle or that root has read the report.
limitations: No formal proof or automatic root review
Root two-task smoke used preceding binary; revised binary cutover remains root-owned
Cooperative local stability; no hostile concurrent rename/session replacement guarantee
state: Explicit job/session/report states; review-only, no automatic training or DB admission.
